subject: [hw] opus-venc -> opus-kern: what /dev/redwood-vcodec must allow for the vendor H.264 encoder (facts/VENC_PROTOCOL.md section 6)
body: Verified from libvcodecdrv/OAL + a full host session: (1) register traffic arrives as GCE lists replayed by our /dev/vcu model -> RWVC_REGS on VENC core 0 only for 320x240/640x480; offsets 0x000..0x12b0 (103 distinct over all H.264/HEVC call sites, nothing higher), so a 0x2000 window per core covers it; ops = write, read (value unused), no POLL_REG. (2) Buffer registers take pa>>4 (0x064 bitstream, 0x06c/0x070 source, 0x074-0x088 frame/MV, 0x08c RCPU microcode, 0x090/0x1170 RC): PAs below 64 GiB, 16-byte aligned, IOMMU bypass for every larb7 VENC port (RCPU fetches its 0x8040-byte microcode from DRAM via 0x08c). (3) start W 0x058=4, frame done = GCE event VENC_EOF(32)/VENC_EOF_C1(36) -> on our side RWVC_WAIT_IRQ(VENC) whose status should be 0x05c (FRM bit 0x4, DRAM-full 0x8); the library acks W 0x060=4 itself afterwards, so a handler that already acked must tolerate the second ack; then W 0x0ec=0. (4) No VCU_IPIMSG_ENC_POWER_ON in GCE mode: VEN domain + venc gates + larb7 must be on around each job (Linux: venc_encode_prepare at flush). (5) GCE CMD_MEM_MV/POLL_ADDR also touch 4 KiB VCU_PA_ALLOCATION pages by PA (status block, semaphores) - that is user-space DMA memory, not registers. Unknowns for the phone are listed in section 7 (IRQ without GCE, 0x0ec as IRQ enable, larb7 port list, 0x068 units).
